claims.text: Large language models excel at numerical estimation.
Large language models struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty.
Large language models are systematically overconfident when constructing confidence intervals around their own answers.
Nominal 99% confidence intervals generated by modern LLMs cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average.
A conformal prediction based approach that adjusts confidence intervals obtains accurate 99% observed coverage in LLMs.
A conformal prediction based approach decreases the Winkler interval score by 54%.
Direct log-probability elicitation reduces LLM overconfidence at high confidence levels.
Quantile adjustment methods reduce LLM overconfidence at high confidence levels.
When reasoning under uncertainty, LLMs exhibit overconfidence by acting as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred distribution and neglecting its tails.

evidence.description: Large language models (LLMs) excel at numerical estimation
but struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty.
We study how well LLMs construct confidence intervals around their own answers and find that they are systematically overconfident.
Across several modern models, nominal 99% intervals cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average.
With a conformal prediction based approach that adjusts the intervals, we obtain accurate 99% observed coverage
and the Winkler interval score decreases by 54%.
We also propose direct log-probability elicitation... which further reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.
and quantile adjustment methods, which further reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.

perception-tunnel theory explaining why LLMs exhibit overconfidence: when reasoning under uncertainty, they act as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred distribution, neglecting its tails.

methodologies.name: FermiEval
methodologies.description: A benchmark of Fermi-style estimation questions evaluated with a scoring rule for confidence interval coverage and sharpness.

methodologies.name: Conformal prediction based interval adjustment
methodologies.description: An adjustment method applied to confidence intervals to achieve calibrated observed coverage and improve interval scores.

methodologies.name: Direct log-probability elicitation
methodologies.description: A method proposing direct log-probability extraction from models to reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.

methodologies.name: Quantile adjustment
methodologies.description: A method adjusting quantiles of inferred distributions to mitigate overconfidence at high confidence levels.

limitations.text: LLMs struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty and are systematically overconfident when constructing confidence intervals.
